sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and setup
sections.what: Brings in the tools this file needs: web route helpers, the audit and timeline services, the database access and the request checks for conditions.
sections.why: Needed so the routes can save data, log activity and check input.

sections.name: ConditionsController (part 1)
sections.title: Creating a chronic condition
sections.what: Saves a new condition for the signed-in user, defaulting to active and moderate when those are not given. It then writes an audit entry and adds a diagnosis event to the user's timeline.
sections.why: Likely reason: every new diagnosis should appear on the timeline and be logged for privacy review.
sections.watch_out: The timeline description combines status, severity and notes, so long notes will make that event text long.

sections.name: ConditionsController (part 2)
sections.title: Listing and updating conditions
sections.what: Lists the user's active conditions, newest diagnosis first, optionally filtered by status. The update route changes status, severity, resolved date, notes or plan, and it logs the change.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. Listing is also logged, which suggests every view of health data is recorded.
sections.watch_out: Listing writes an audit entry on every call, so the audit table will grow quickly with heavy use.

sections.name: ConditionsController (part 3)
sections.title: Resolving and deleting conditions
sections.what: When a condition is marked resolved, adds a resolved event to the timeline. Delete hides the condition by setting a deleted date and only logs the deletion if a record was actually hidden.
sections.why: Keeps the timeline in step with the condition and keeps old records for history rather than erasing them.
sections.watch_out: The resolved event is only added when the status is RESOLVED in the request, so a resolved date sent alone does not create one.

summary: Lets a signed-in user record, list, update and soft-delete their own chronic conditions such as diabetes or hypertension.
purpose: Stores a user's long-term health conditions and keeps a matching entry on their health timeline.
why: Reason not stated in the code. The soft delete suggests records are kept for history.
how: Each route reads the signed-in user from the token. Create saves the condition, writes an audit entry and adds a timeline event. List returns non-deleted conditions, optionally filtered by status. Update checks the condition belongs to the user, saves changes, and adds a resolved timeline event when status becomes RESOLVED. Delete marks the record as deleted and audits it.
inputs: Request bodies from CreateConditionDto and UpdateConditionDto, an optional status filter, the condition id from the URL, and the user id from the token.
outputs: Objects with success and data, or a not-found message. List returns a data array.
risks: Health data is written and read here, so every route must keep the user id check. Errors are not caught, so a failing database call returns a server error.
debug: Check the audit records and the timeline table when a change looks missing. If an update returns not found, confirm the condition is not already soft-deleted. Check the database connection if every route fails.
